newsitem.title: USA: Seven Seas tests 3-zone Colombia well.
newsitem.headline: Seven Seas tests 3-zone Colombia well.

text.p: Seven Seas Petroleum Inc said on Monday that preliminary testing at its El Segundo No 2 well in Colombia yielded oil and gas production from three intervals in the upper Cretaceous Cimarrona formation.
Seven Seas said a limestone interval between 6,054 and 6,142 feet tested at 5,340 barrels per day of oil and 610 thousand cubic feet per day of gas.
A limestone and sandstone interval between 6,142 and 6,222 feet tested at 6,154 BPD of oil and 620 MCFD of gas.
A sandstone interval between 6,236 and 6,280 feet tested at 3,866 BPD of oil and 493 MCFD of gas.
The company said the production rates were limited by the capabilities of the testing equipment.

It said it planned a combined rate test from 6,054 to about 6,315 feet to determine the overall productive capacity of the section in the well and expected to release the results of the new test within 12 days.
The company then expected to start as soon as possible the Tres Pasos No 1 well, 2.5 km northwest of El Segundo No 2.
Seven Seas is operator and holds a 51.7 percent stake in the prospect. It expects a deal that would add another six percent to its interest to be concluded within the next two weeks.
Other partners include Chile's state oil company and a private investor in Oklahoma City, a company spokesman said. ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
